title: A real longitudinal patient cohort: the ecosystem's mixed-model wrapper reproduces lme4 exactly on 6 months of Parkinson's UPDRS telemonitoring

dataset.name: Oxford Parkinson's Disease Telemonitoring
dataset.version: UCI Machine Learning Repository id 189 (Tsanas et al. 2010)
dataset.record: 42 early-stage Parkinson's patients; ~5875 biweekly voice recordings over ~6 months (~140/subject); 16 dysphonia features plus age/sex and clinician-scored motor_UPDRS/total_UPDRS, tracked longitudinally by test_time (days since recruitment)
dataset.citation: Tsanas A, Little MA, McSharry PE, Ramig LO. Accurate telemonitoring of Parkinson's disease progression by non-invasive speech tests. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2010;57(4):884-893. Data: UCI ML Repository id 189, doi:10.24432/C5ZS3N (CC BY 4.0).

proposition: On a REAL 42-patient longitudinal cohort, PhysioClinStats::fitMixedModel reproduces the reference mixed-model engine lme4::lmer EXACTLY: fitting total_UPDRS ~ test_time + age + sex + PPE + (1 | subject), the two engines' fixed effects agree to machine precision (max absolute difference = 0) and their random-intercept SD is identical (10.07 UPDRS points). PhysioCore::PhysioCohort represents the 42-subject container end-to-end and PhysioClinStats::doseResponse runs on it. Over the ~6-month window total UPDRS drifts upward (+0.019 points/day) -- the expected slow progression direction. This validates the longitudinal-cohort analysis chain on genuine patient data via the same 'recover the reference engine' bar the ecosystem meets elsewhere.

claims.statement: Parkinson's patients in the longitudinal telemonitoring cohort
voice recordings analysed (repeated measures over ~6 months)
subject random-intercept SD, identical across both engines (UPDRS points)
total-UPDRS change per day (> 0 = progression over the ~6 months)
subjects in the PhysioCohort container built end-to-end

validation.reference: The reference mixed-model engine lme4::lmer (Bates, Machler, Bolker, Walker 2015, J Stat Softw 67:1-48) fitting total_UPDRS ~ test_time + age + sex + PPE + (1 | subject). A correct wrapper must reproduce its fixed-effect estimates and random-intercept SD to numeric precision -- the same 'recover the reference engine' criterion the ecosystem meets for JMLE vs eRm and ENMO vs GGIR.
validation.data: REAL -- UCI Parkinson's Telemonitoring (Tsanas et al. 2010), 42 early-stage PD patients, ~5875 biweekly voice recordings over ~6 months, motor_/total_UPDRS tracked with test_time (days since recruitment); CC BY 4.0.
validation.note: The reproducible result is EXACT reference-engine agreement: fitMixedModel reproduces lme4::lmer's fixed effects (max abs diff = 0) and random-intercept SD (10.07 UPDRS points) on this real longitudinal patient cohort, PhysioCohort represents the 42-subject container, and doseResponse runs on it. Honest scope: (1) this is VOICE telemonitoring, not gait/rehab -- but it is the realistic genuinely-longitudinal, fully-downloadable, public patient cohort with a tracked clinical outcome (serial-Fugl-Meyer stroke-rehab cohorts are DUA-gated and fail the public-data bar); (2) UPDRS is a SUMMARY score, so item-level Rasch / scoreCohort byte-exact reproduction is not available from this dataset; (3) the +0.019 UPDRS/day test_time slope is reported as a demonstrated progression DIRECTION, not validated against an external landmark. The validated claim is the reference-engine reproduction -- a true numeric validation on real patient data.

open_questions.q: A truly longitudinal STROKE-REHAB cohort with serial Fugl-Meyer (for proportionalRecoveryRule / item-level Rasch byte-exact validation) is almost always access-controlled (DUA) and fails the public-data gate; this public PD voice cohort is the honest ceiling for a fully-downloadable longitudinal patient cohort. Documented, not escalated.
